title: A Characterisation of Economic Romanticism
author: V.I. Lenin
shortDescription: Lenin's comprehensive critique of Sismondi and Russian Narodism, dismantling petty-bourgeois romantic economics and demonstrating how capitalism develops the home market through the ruination of subsistence producers.
subject: Political Economy and Critique of Romanticism
context: Written in Siberian exile in the spring of 1897 and published in the journal Novoye Slovo, this work served as the theoretical groundwork for Lenin's monumental study The Development of Capitalism in Russia (1899), systematically demolishing Narodnik claims that capitalism could not develop in Russia.
relatesToToday: Provides critical arguments against modern degrowth romanticism, 'small is beautiful' localism, and moralistic critiques of capitalism that dream of returning to pre-industrial artisanal production rather than socializing advanced productive forces under workers' democratic control.
keyTakeaways: The home market expands through proletarianization: The ruination of subsistence peasant farming does not destroy the home market; it creates it by turning subsistence food and tools into market commodities and forcing peasants into wage labor.

Adam Smith's dogma refuted: Classical economics and romanticists wrongly omitted constant capital (c) from total product; Marx showed that Department I (means of production) creates a massive internal market that realizes accumulation.

Underconsumption is not the ultimate cause of crises: Crises do not stem from workers' low consumption (which exists in all class societies), but from the anarchy of production and the fundamental contradiction between socialized production and private appropriation.

Progressive nature of machine industry: While machinery brings temporary displacement under capitalism, it massively raises labor productivity, breaks patriarchal backwardness, and creates the material basis for socialism.

Scientific critique versus romantic reaction: Scientific socialism criticizes capitalism from the forward-looking standpoint of the revolutionary proletariat, whereas economic romanticism measures modern industry with the backward-looking yardstick of patriarchal small production.
